t: Baybars succeeds Qutuz as Mamluk sultan
c: On the way back to Egypt after the battle, Qutuz died and was succeeded by another commander, Baybars, who assumed the sultanate and ruled from 1260 to 1277.

t: Cairo becomes center of Islamic world
c: Due to the sack of Baghdad by the Mongols in 1258, Cairo became the central city of the Islamic world.

t: Tulunid forces defeat Ibn Kundādj; peace treaties follow
c: From 885 to 886, the Tulunid forces, led by Khumarawayh, defeated Ibn Kundād̲j, though the latter had superior numbers.

c: In 786 CE, al-Rashid appointed Abu Salim Faraj al-Khadim al-Turki to oversee the reconstruction and completion of the city of Tarsus.

c: Subsequently, Nuh dispatched him as a gift to the Abbasid Caliph al-Ma'mun, accompanied by other Turkic Mamluks, in the year 200 AH (816 CE).

t: Caliphate troops sent against Ibn Tulun for tribute arrears
c: In 877, troops of the caliphate were sent against him, due to his insufficient payment of tribute.

t: Ibn Harun assassinated
c: However, Ibn Harun was assassinated at the banks of the Tigris River in 260 AH (874 AD) before assuming his new position.

t: Ahmad ibn Tulun departs Al-Qata'i for Ramla
c: In Shawwal 264 AH (June 878 AD), Ahmad ibn Tulun departed from Al-Qata'i and proceeded to Ramla, where he was met by the city's governor, Muhammad ibn Rafi'.

t: Revolt of Isa ibn al-Shaykh in Palestine
c: The need for the establishment of an autonomous armed force became apparent after the revolt of ʿĪsā ibn al-Shaykkh, governor of Palestine, in 870.

t: Ibn Tulun's forces swear personal allegiance
c: In a ceremony held in 871, Ibn Tulun had his forces swear personal allegiance to him.

t: First treaty with al-Muwaffaq establishes financial provisions
c: Financial provisions were made in the first treaty in 886 with al-Muwaffak.

t: Second treaty with al-Muʿtaḍid reaffirms political terms
c: A second treaty with al-Muʿtaḍid, the son of al-Muwaffak, in 892, re-affirmed the political terms of the first.

t: Muhammad ibn Ra'iq takes over Syria
c: Muhammad ibn Ra'iq took over Syria in 939, which threatened Egypt.

t: Ibn Tughj family awarded governorships for thirty years
c: In 944, the governorships of Egypt, Syria and Hijaz were awarded for 30 years to ibn Tughj's family, and these posts would pass to his son, Abu'l-Qasim.

c: Only a later attempt by the Fatimid general Jawhar al-Siqilli managed to conquer Egypt in 969.

t: Idrisid princes of Fez submit to Umayyads
c: From 949 the Idrisid princes of Fez and the Banu Ifran of Tlemcen had submitted to the Umayyads.

t: Constantine VII besieges Naples
c: In 956, Emperor Constantine VII sent the patrician Argirius to besiege Naples, an ally of the Muslims.

t: Byzantine army captures Taormina in Sicily
c: However, the Byzantine attack on Crete resumed hostilities and a new army led by Ammar besieged Taormina, capturing it in 962.

t: Nikephoros Phokas sends army to reconquer Sicily
c: In 964 Emperor Nikephoros Phokas sent a 40,000-man army under his nephew Manuel and the admiral Niketas to reconquer Sicily.

t: Ya'qub ibn Killis elevated to vizier
c: The first to be appointed to this position was the Jewish convert Ya'qub ibn Killis, who was elevated to this office in 979 by al-Mu'izz's successor al-Aziz.

t: John Tzimisces retakes Palestine and Syria
c: In 975, the Byzantine emperor John Tzimisces retook most of Palestine and Syria, leaving only Tripoli in Fatimid control.

t: Fatimid forces take Homs and Hama
c: He took Homs and Hama in 992 and defeated a combined force from Hamdanid Aleppo and Byzantine-held Antioch.

t: Umayyads reassert authority in northern Morocco
c: After Jawhar's successful western expedition, the Umayyads returned to northern Morocco in 973 to reassert their authority.

t: Al-Mansur moves Zirid dynasty base to al-Mansuriyya

t: Al-Hakim assassinates Barjawan and takes control
c: In the year 1000, Barjawan was assassinated by al-Hakim, who now took direct and autocratic control of the state.

t: Abu Rakwa uprising suppressed near Cairo
c: In 1005, during his early reign, a dangerous uprising led by Abu Rakwa was successfully put down but had come within striking distance of Cairo.

t: Anushtakin defeats Bedouins at Battle of Uqhuwana
c: Al-Jarjara'i sent Anushtakin al-Dizbari, a Turkish commander, with a force that defeated them in 1029 at the Battle of Uqhuwana near Lake Tiberias.

t: Romanos III invades northern Syria
c: In 1030 the new Byzantine emperor Romanos III broke a truce to invade northern Syria and forced Aleppo to recognise his suzerainty.

t: Al-Mustansir becomes caliph
c: Al-Zahir died in 1036 and was succeeded by his son, al-Mustansir, who had the longest reign in Fatimid history, serving as caliph from 1036 to 1094.

t: Campaign to conquer Yemen begins
c: In 1060, he began a campaign to conquer all of Yemen, capturing Aden and Zabid.

t: Juyushi Mosque completed under Badr
c: The Juyushi Mosque ('the Mosque of the Armies'), was commissioned by Badr and completed in 1085 under the patronage of the caliph.

t: Badr al-Jamali and al-Mustansir die
c: Badr al-Jamali died in 1094, along with Caliph al-Mustansir that same year, and his son Al-Afdal Shahanshah succeeded him in power as vizier.

t: Ibn Sallar installed as vizier
c: After negotiating with the women of the palace, Ibn Sallar was installed as vizier in 1150.

t: Nasr murders al-Zafir; al-Fa'iz becomes caliph
c: The next year (1154), Nasr murdered al-Zafir, and Abbas, now vizier, declared his 5-year-old son Isa (al-Fa'iz) the new caliph.

t: Al-Fa'iz dies; Tala'i assassinated
c: Al-Fa'iz died in 1160 and Tala'i was assassinated in 1161 by Sitt al-Qusur, a sister of al-Zafir.

t: Shawar overthrows Ruzzik ibn Tala'i
c: Tala'i's son, Ruzzik ibn Tala'i, held the office of vizier until 1163, when he was overthrown and killed by Shawar, the governor of Qus.

c: When Shawar was driven out of Cairo by Dirgham in 1163, he sought refuge and help with Nur al-Din.

t: Crusaders pursue Shirkuh's forces into Upper Egypt
c: In 1167, the Crusaders pursued Shirkuh's forces into Upper Egypt.

t: Al-Mahdiyya established as Fatimid capital
c: Al-Mahdiyya, the first capital of the Fatimid dynasty, was established by its first caliph, Abdullah al-Mahdi in 300 AH/912–913 CE.

t: Al-Mansuriyya established near Kairouan by al-Mansur

t: Zirids abandon al-Mansuriyya for Mahdiyya
c: In 1057, under pressure from the Banu Hilal invasions, the Zirids abandoned al-Mansuriyya for Mahdiyya and the city was devastated.

t: Saladin proclaimed Sultan of Egypt, expands sultanate

t: Saladin defeats Crusaders at Battle of Hattin
c: Most of the Crusader states fell to Saladin after his victory at the Battle of Hattin in 1187, but the Crusaders reconquered the Syrian coastlands in the 1190s.

t: Saladin dies; al-Adil becomes sultan
c: After Saladin's death in 1193, his sons contested control of the sultanate, but Saladin's brother al-Adil ultimately became sultan in 1200.

t: Al-Mu'azzam Turanshah succeeds as-Salih Ayyub
c: After his death in 1249, as-Salih Ayyub was succeeded in Egypt by his son al-Mu'azzam Turanshah.

t: Ayyub and Shirkuh flee Tikrit
c: The Abbasid court issued arrest warrants for both Ayyub and Shirkuh, but before the brothers could be arrested, they departed Tikrit for Mosul in 1138.

t: Shirkuh becomes vizier after Shawar's death
c: Shawar died in 1169 and Shirkuh became vizier, but he too died later that year.

t: Almohad caliph Yaqub al-Mansur reconquers Ifriqiya
c: The Almohad caliph Yaqub al-Mansur reconquered Ifriqiya from 1187 to 1188, defeating both of them.

t: Saladin sends Turan-Shah to conquer Yemen and Hejaz
c: In 1173, Saladin sent Turan-Shah to conquer Yemen and the Hejaz.

c: By 1175, he had taken control of Hama and Homs but failed to take Aleppo after besieging it.

t: Shirkuh's descendants receive control of Homs
c: Control of Homs was handed to the descendants of Shirkuh in 1179 and Hama was given to Saladin's nephew, al-Muzaffar Umar.

t: Mas'ud of Mosul and Zangi II form Zengid coalition
c: In 1193, Mas'ud of Mosul joined forces with Zangi II of Sinjar and together the Zengid coalition moved to conquer al-Jazira.

t: Qatada ibn Idris becomes emir of Mecca

t: Kingdom of Georgia challenges Ayyubid rule in Anatolia
c: By 1208 Kingdom of Georgia challenged Ayyubid rule in eastern Anatolia and besieged Khilat (possessions of al-Awhad).

t: Crusaders besiege fortress of Damietta

t: Nur ad-Din Umar declares independence
c: Following Mas'ud ibn Kamil's death in 1229, Nur ad-Din Umar declared his independence and discontinued the annual tribute payment to the Ayyubids in Egypt.

t: Al-Kamil and Frederick sign truce
c: Al-Kamil continued negotiations with Frederick in Acre in 1228, leading to a truce signed in February 1229.

t: As-Salih Ayyub installed to govern Hisn Kayfa

An-Nasir Yusuf decides to annex Homs
c: An-Nasir Yusuf found this intolerable and decided to annex Homs in the winter of 1248.

t: Bahri Mamluks revolt and kill sultan
c: Fearing for their positions of power, the Bahri Mamluks revolted against the sultan and killed him in April 1250.
